# Taxonomy of Grid-Based Logic Games

## I. PLACEMENT GAMES
Games where you place objects, numbers, or marks in cells

### A. Light/Illumination
- **Akari** - Place light bulbs that illuminate rows/columns

### B. Number Placement
- **Sudoku** - Place numbers 1-9 in rows, columns, and blocks
- **Nansuke** - Fill blank cells with numbers from a list
- **Makaro** - Fill cells with numbers based on directional arrows
- **Ripple Effect** - Fill rooms with consecutive numbers starting from 1
- **Kurotto** - Color cells based on number sums extending from circles

### C. Block/Shape Placement
- **Shikaku** - Divide grid into rectangles containing one number
- **Fillomino** - Fill blocks with numbers matching block size
- **Chained Block** - Fill blocks with numbers, forming chains
- **Choco Banana** - Paint cells black to form rectangles/squares
- **Double Choco** - Divide grid into blocks with matching white/gray pairs
- **LITS** - Color four-cell tetrominoes in each region
- **Nuritwin** - Shade two equal-sized blocks per region
- **Sashigane** - Divide grid into L-shaped blocks
- **Shakashaka** - Place black triangles to form white rectangles/squares
- **Sto-stone** - Color cells so stones fill bottom half when dropped

### D. Snake/Path Placement
- **Hebi** - Place numbers 1-5 forming connected snakes
- **Pencils** - Draw lines from pencil tips using length numbers
- **Evolomino** - Place squares on arrows, growing by one cell per block

### E. Circle/Object Movement
- **Satogaeri** - Move circles so each country contains one
- **Yosenabe** - Move circles into gray areas with matching sums

---

## II. COLORING/SHADING GAMES
Games where you color or shade cells

### A. Black Cell Coloring
- **Kurodoko** - Color cells black based on distance to nearest black cell
- **Hitori** - Color cells to eliminate duplicate numbers in rows/columns
- **Nurikabe** - Color cells black to form continuous wall, separating white regions
- **Nurimisaki** - Color cells black around white "Misaki" promontories
- **Usowan** - Color cells based on neighbor count (with one wrong number per region)
- **Tilepaint** - Color tiles based on diagonal cell counts
- **Heyawake** - Color cells in rooms based on given numbers

### B. Mixed Coloring
- **Norinori** - Color two black squares per region
- **Nurimeizu** - Color cells to create maze from S to G

---

## III. LINE-DRAWING GAMES
Games where you draw continuous loops or paths

### A. Single Loop Games
- **Slitherlink** - Connect dots to form loop based on number clues
- **Masyu** - Draw loop through circles with specific turn rules
- **Dotchi-Loop** - Draw loop through white circles with turn constraints
- **Mid-loop** - Draw loop with black circles as midpoints
- **Moon-or-Sun** - Draw loop alternating between moon/sun cells per room
- **Yajilin** - Draw loop avoiding black cells indicated by arrows
- **Nagareru** - Draw loop following directional arrows with wind effects
- **Suraromu** - Draw loop starting/ending at numbered circle, passing gates

### B. Path/Connection Games
- **Numberlink** - Connect pairs of same numbers with non-crossing lines
- **Hashiwokakero** - Connect islands with bridges (1-2 per pair)

---

## IV. DIVISION/PARTITIONING GAMES
Games where you divide the grid into regions

### A. Region Division
- **Five Cells** - Divide grid into five-cell blocks with line constraints
- **Juosan** - Fill cells with — or | marks in territories with difference counts

---

## V. HYBRID GAMES
Games combining multiple mechanics

- **Pencils** - Placement + line-drawing (lines from pencil tips)
- **Evolomino** - Placement + path-following (growing blocks on arrows)

---

## Summary by Primary Mechanic

| Mechanic | Count | Examples |
|----------|-------|----------|
| **Placement** | 17 | Sudoku, Shikaku, Fillomino, LITS, Shakashaka, etc. |
| **Coloring** | 8 | Kurodoko, Hitori, Nurikabe, Tilepaint, etc. |
| **Line-Drawing** | 8 | Slitherlink, Masyu, Yajilin, Suraromu, etc. |
| **Division** | 2 | Five Cells, Juosan |
| **Hybrid** | 2 | Pencils, Evolomino |
